reference: GNU util-linux taskset from the runner's read-only /usr tree is the independent oracle for parse-time error cases. Bash builtin type/help output and the documented taskset loadable contract are checked as contract cases. Kernel affinity operations are deliberately deferred.
coverage: Bash builtin registration and taskset help documentation
GNU taskset rejection of malformed hexadecimal masks and descending CPU ranges
GNU taskset rejection of an overflowing PID without producing query output
exclusions: Affinity query, affinity mutation, and command-wrapper syscalls are deferred because they require deterministic permitted CPU sets and a controlled process fixture; no such operation is claimed to have passed.

cases.purpose: Verify taskset is registered as a Bash builtin and its Bash help retains the documented synopsis and CPU mask/list contract.
cases.script:
[[ $(type -t taskset) == builtin ]] || exit 1
doc=$(help taskset) || exit 1
case $doc in *"Run or query commands with a CPU affinity mask."*) ;; *) exit 1 ;; esac
case $doc in *"taskset [-c] -p PID"*) ;; *) exit 1 ;; esac
case $doc in *"MASK is hexadecimal, with optional 0x prefix."*) ;; *) exit 1 ;; esac
case $doc in *"With -c/--cpu-list,"*) ;; *) exit 1 ;; esac
case $doc in *"affinity values are CPU lists such as 0,2-3."*) ;; *) exit 1 ;; esac
printf 'builtin\nhelp-contract-ok\n'

cases.purpose: Check the loadable's documented --help text, including supported query, set, wrapper and CPU-list forms.
cases.stdout:
taskset — taskset(1) subset over sched_getaffinity/sched_setaffinity
usage: taskset [-c] -p PID
       taskset [-c] -p MASK|LIST PID
       taskset [-c] MASK|LIST COMMAND [ARG...]
       taskset --help | --version

MASK is a hexadecimal CPU affinity mask, with optional 0x prefix.
-c/--cpu-list treats affinity values as CPU lists such as 0,2-3.

cases.purpose: Check the version string documented by the documented taskset interface.
GNU taskset rejects a non-hexadecimal mask before attempting to start the relative command; compare its failure status and empty stdout.
GNU taskset rejects a descending CPU range while parsing -c input, before attempting to start the relative command.
Check GNU taskset's parse-time rejection of an overflowing PID and verify no affinity-query output is produced.
Query one controlled process in both hexadecimal-mask and CPU-list forms, then verify both describe the same affinity.
cases.reason: Requires a disposable VM or reviewed syscall mock with a fixed allowed CPU set, a live owned fixture process, and GNU util-linux taskset. The future fixture should verify exact PID-tagged output and independently encode mask/list equivalence; the controller's ambient CPU set is not a stable expected value.

cases.purpose: Set affinity on an owned helper process with -p and verify its reported and effective affinity afterward.
cases.reason: Requires a disposable VM or reviewed syscall mock with a helper child owned by the fixture and at least two known permitted CPUs. The future comparison must check GNU taskset's old/new output and independently query the child's resulting affinity; this suite does not mutate a process affinity.

cases.purpose: Exercise mask and CPU-list command-wrapper forms with a controlled executable, including argv/stdout and child exit-status propagation.
cases.reason: Requires a disposable VM or reviewed sched_setaffinity mock with a deterministic permitted CPU set and a controlled executable probe. The future fixture should cover hexadecimal and -c list inputs, successful and rejected affinity requests, preserved arguments/output, and the child's exit status. No affinity-setting wrapper operation is claimed to have passed here.
